verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Both equality tests the dispatch names pass by ==, and so does every other string the catalog carries: namedCorpusNotAuthored, the class id, memberVerbatim, slashJoiner, exactByteIntent at 1026 characters and passProperty at 350 characters are each character-equal to live G22 v1. The live class object has exactly five keys and all five are carried, so completeness is structural rather than a judgement call, and the two added fields — fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED and filesystemSelectorPopulated false — are negative markers that populate nothing. All 11 cited path/digest pairs measure equal with zero mismatches, and recordedInputs.HEAD agrees with the top-level head and live HEAD as the artifact's own invariant requires. Closure is not merely denied but structurally unavailable: the artifact carries no whatThisCloses-style field, and the pinned leftover-join still holds OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-RESERVED-TABLES at leftoverDesign true. Nothing is populated, nothing is applied, no DR-G* row is added, required-now is 26, and the subject did not move. Four further refutations of my own — an invented fixture identifier, a smuggled D-006 unit or byte constant, an overstated cited standing, and over-quantification across filesystems or platforms — all failed against live bytes. The identifier probe is the one worth naming: a catalog is precisely the artifact type that would coin an id, and live G22 v1's own note forbids it, but the single id here measures == equal to the live one, so none is coined.
